content: I'll read the test image to analyze the plant disease symptoms.

**Visual Analysis:**

- **Affected part:** Leaf (tomato or similar solanaceous plant)
- **Spot characteristics:** Numerous small, dark brown to black spots scattered irregularly across the entire upper leaf surface
- **Pattern:** No clear concentric rings (rules out Early Blight/Target Spot)
- **Texture:** No powdery coating (rules out Powdery Mildew), no velvety mold (rules out Leaf Mold)
- **Leaf distortion:** Some puckering/wrinkling visible at the leaf margins
- **Spot size:** Small, roughly 1–3mm, irregular, some coalescing

**Reasoning through candidates:**

- **Early Blight**: Ruled out — no concentric "target" rings
- **Septoria_Leaf_Blotch**: Spots would have tan/gray centers with dark border and pycnidia; spots here are uniformly dark
- **Target_Spot**: Ruled out — no star/X cracking or distinct concentric rings
- **Tomato_Spotted_Wilt_Virus**: TSWV causes bronze/necrotic ring spots and leaf distortion — the numerous small dark spots and slight leaf puckering are consistent
- **Bacterial_Speck_Of_Tomato**: Small (1–2mm), dark brown to black spots, very numerous, scattered — highly characteristic match for the dense distribution of small dark spots seen here

The spots are very small, densely scattered, and uniformly dark brown/black — most consistent with **Bacterial_Speck_Of_Tomato** (Pseudomonas syringae pv. tomato), which classically presents as numerous tiny dark lesions across leaf surfaces.
